page: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon TDX processor operating at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, backed by 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. The underlying processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache, along with hardware extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance includes no local storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on remote block storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the EC2es_v6 demonstrates competitive single-threaded execution due to its high base frequency, scoring 1943.0 on the Geekbench single-core benchmark and 1904.76 on stress-ng single-core tests. However, total parallel compute capacity is constrained by the two-vCPU ceiling. Multi-core performance metrics, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 2182.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3670.32, position the instance in the lower percentiles compared across broader multi-core categories. Redis throughput reached 2.58 million SET operations per second, while database and memory test metrics reflect the limitations of the single physical core.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the EC2es_v6 provides an economical path to acquiring 16 GB of memory without requiring payment for excess compute cores. The absence of local disk hardware reduces host-level storage overhead but necessitates network-attached storage integration. Given its high memory density paired with entry-level parallel execution capacity, the instance is suited for lightweight caching tiers, small in-memory datastores, and memory-intensive background tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance comprises 1 physical core with 2 threads, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache and instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. No local disks or GPU accelerators are included. Benchmark evaluations reflect strong single-core capabilities, registering 1943.0 on Geekbench single-core, but parallel throughput is constrained by the limited core count, as seen in lower multi-core Geekbench and PassMark scores. Redis throughput achieves 2.58 million SET operations per second. With high memory per core and moderate computational capacity, EC2es_v6 is tailored for memory-bound workloads with low parallel processing demands, such as small in-memory datastores, lightweight caching tiers, and memory-centric microservices.
